To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) in the absence of matter, there are no physical observables in general relativity; (ii) the presence of a physical reference system allows one to identify physical observables in a gauge invariant way; (iii) the presence of physical observables allows one to identify the physical spacetime points; (iv) the physical spacetime is not the mathematical spacetime, but a physical object that is defined in a gauge invariant manner.
the physical observables of the model are the gauge invariant functionals of the fields, and that the physical spacetime points are the points of the physical manifold.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the identification of the observables of a diffeomorphism-invariant theory is a nontrivial issue that cannot be bypassed by simply declaring that the observables of the theory are the diffeomorphism invariants.
the identification of physical spacetime point is not possible a priori, but requires an analysis of the physical system.

the problem of the definition of the physical spacetime is not solved by the introduction of the concept of quantum geometry, but it requires a deeper understanding of the physical meaning of the quantum gravitational variables.
